subject: Post-call: quantify token bands & dedicated GPU options
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novushealth.ai>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: token bands and dedicated GPU options (quick clarifications)

Hi Priya (and Ben),

Great call this morning — thanks for the walkthrough of Redwood Dedicated. A couple quick items we promised to capture so we can move toward a committed pilot:

- Our rough usage profile: 4M tokens/day (peaks up to ~6M), so roughly 120M tokens/month as a baseline.
- Our budget band for unit economics: targeting roughly $150–$230 per 1M tokens (we're flexible within that range if we can reduce tail latency and get predictable costs).
- Preferred HW: we prefer H100 lanes for latency headroom, but will consider A100 if the $/1M economics materially improve.
- Desired throughput/latency: need ~100–140 concurrent requests (avg ~45 tokens/req); p50 latency target ~<200ms on typical prompts.

Questions for Redwood to confirm next:
1) Can you sketch two reserved SKU options (H100 x4 and A100 x8 as examples) showing expected $/1M tokens and an estimated monthly spend?
2) Do you have quantization/precision options we should consider that materially lower $/1M without breaking quality? (we can share sample prompts if helpful)
3) Ideal procurement timeline: we’re aiming for a pilot in ~6 weeks if pricing and SLOs look good.

Appreciate a short recap + any attachments (unit econ spreadsheet, SKU options) and next steps.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of ML Infrastructure, Novus Health
[Attachment: Novus-usage-estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novushealth.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: token bands and dedicated GPU options (quick clarifications)

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear summary and for joining the call. Quick recap and clarifying Qs below; I’ve attached a lightweight CSV with a few scenarios so you can see how we model unit econ.

Recap (baseline you gave):
- Baseline: 4M tokens/day (peaks 6M) → ~120M tokens/mo
- Target $/1M tokens: $150–$230
- Preferred HW: H100 preferred; open to A100 if it reduces cost per token
- Throughput SLO: ~100–140 concurrent requests, avg 45 tokens/req, p50 <200ms

What we’ll deliver next (by EOD tomorrow):
- Two SKU options with conservative token throughput estimates and per-1M token unit-costs: (1) 4x H100 reserved; (2) 8x A100 reserved. We’ll include an option that assumes 4-bit quantization where feasible.
- A short unit-econ workbook (attached) showing assumptions: avg tokens/req, GPU utilization, batching benefits, KV/prefix cache impact.
- A suggested pilot cadence and required legal/procurement checklist to hit your ~6-week pilot target.

Clarifying Qs to help our sizing:
1) Are most requests single-turn or multi-turn sessions with long context? (multi-turn increases KV cache pressure)
2) Do you have a 95th/99th percentile token-length estimate for production traffic (or a sample prompt set we can run quickly)?

Attachments: token-econ-scenarios.csv (simple assumptions), note: we’ll follow up with the full XLSX and a PDF with SKU estimates.

If you prefer, we can run a short perf validation on a representative prompt set this week — Ben can help coordinate.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0132
[Attachment: token-econ-scenarios.csv (spreadsheet)]

From: Sofia Martin <sofia.martin@novushealth.ai>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: daniel.park@novushealth.ai, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: token bands and dedicated GPU options (quick clarifications)

Thanks Priya — quick answers from our side:

- Session shape: about 70% single-turn inference (short prompts), 30% multi-turn (avg 6 turns, mostly for triage workflows).
- Token length: median 38 tokens/req; p95 ~220 tokens/req.
- Quality vs. cost: we can tolerate 4-bit quantization on non-latency-critical paths; for the triage multi-turn flows we’d prefer FP16/Half precision to avoid subtle quality regressions.
- Procurement timing: legal is ok to move on a pilot MSA; budget owner wants to see two firm SKU estimates with $/1M token anchors before approving commitment.

Happy to share a small sample set of prompts (anonymized) — will drop a link later today.

— Sofia

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martin <sofia.martin@novushealth.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@novushealth.ai>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: token bands and dedicated GPU options (next steps & SKUs)

Hi Sofia + Daniel — thanks for the quick turn. Per Priya’s note, attaching two SKU options and a unit-econ workbook. TL;DR up front:

Option A (performance-focused)
- 4x H100 reserved lanes (dedicated)
- Estimated effective throughput: accommodates baseline + 25% headroom for peak (approx 6M tokens/day) with p50 ~140ms on median prompt lengths
- Estimated unit cost: ~$210 per 1M tokens (assumes FP16 for multi-turn triage flows)

Option B (cost-focused)
- 8x A100 reserved lanes (higher aggregate capacity, lower per-GPU cost)
- Estimated effective throughput: higher batching efficiency, target supports your 120M/mo baseline comfortably
- Estimated unit cost: ~$165 per 1M tokens (assumes mixed precision + 4-bit quantization on appropriate paths)

Notes & assumptions (see workbook):
- We model batching and prefix caching to reduce per-token GPU cycles; your multi-turn KV cache usage (30% of traffic) reduces tokens processed when sessions are warm.
- We’ve included a sensitivity tab with +/-20% token volume scenarios.
- Pilot plan: 2-week benchmark with your sample prompts → we’ll run end-to-end latency/throughput tests and return a fielded SKU recommendation.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share anonymized prompt set (Sofia mentioned this) — we’ll run a quick perf validation (2–3 business days).
2) We provision a short-lived benchmark cluster (no charge) mirroring Option A and B configs and return the raw traces.
3) We deliver a formal quote (HubSpot linked below) and SoW for a 6–8 week pilot.

Attachments: dedicated-sku-options.pdf, unit-econ-breakdown.xlsx
Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/7841

If that plan works, Priya will coordinate scheduling for the perf run this week.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: dedicated-sku-options.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: unit-econ-breakdown.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
